item.title: Texas Rep. Greg Casar discusses bill to temporarily pause advanced AI development
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with U.S. Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, about his efforts to regulate artificial intelligence.

item.title: The powerful millionaires hiding in plain sight
item.description: They own car dealerships, law firms, dental practices, and restaurant chains. Collectively, these overlooked business owners hold far more wealth than the Forbes 400 — and wield considerable political power.

item.title: Local election officials are training to defend the midterms from interference
item.description: Hundreds of election officials from around the country are meeting to discuss how to defend the integrity of the midterm elections, including against interference by the federal government.federal government.

item.description: President Trump returns to the U.S. ready to rally on behalf of Republican candidates as the midterm election enters its crucial fall stretch.

item.title: Lawmakers home in on midterm messages as Congress returns to session
item.description: Congress returns for a short last session ahead of the midterm election with a full plate as lawmakers look for messaging bills they can take back to voters.

item.title: Trump downplays calls for AI slowdown
item.description: President Trump said the dire warnings about AI were exaggerated and that "negative forces" are making claims about things that won't happen. This comes after leaders in the industry called for putting the brakes on AI development.

item.title: Wisconsin congressman survives emergency plane landing, swims to safety
item.description: Wisconsin Congressman Tom Tiffany escaped a sinking plane and swam to shallow water after an emergency landing in a lake. Tiffany and the pilot called 911 from on top of the plane.

item.title: Politics chat: Trump's $5,000 promise to voters, Vance invokes Charlie Kirk
item.description: Following the midterm convention in Dallas, President Trump's $5,000 campaign promise has generated attention, but not belief. And, Vice President JD Vance characterizes Democrats as extremists.

item.title: The Social Security trust fund is running out. Why is it not a top campaign issue?
item.description: Limited public discussion of the trust fund's shortfall has experts worried that most Americans don't fully understand the problems Social Security faces — or weigh in on solutions.
